title: De vita et gestis Scipionis p'mi Affricani
shelf_note: A 15th-century humanist manuscript of Latin epic verse about Scipio and Carthage. It has no tradition or collection assigned, and it sits outside the library's core esoteric/early-science shelves; at best it is adjacent humanist literature.
structure_note: All three pages are hexameter verse from Petrarch's epic Africa (Hannibal's lament, the battle of Zama: 'Turbine occurrunt alio... Impia carthago rerum tenuisset habenas'). They are not the prose life of Scipio that the title 'De vita et gestis Scipionis' names. The volume may bind both works, but the catalogue title does not describe these pages; possible I7. The leaf numbers 76 and 114 are written in pencil in the corner, and the OCR's page-num picks them up correctly. 308 of 314 pages are translated.

book_verdict: A real Petrarch 'Africa' manuscript, read reasonably well but with meaning-changing misreads (Rex→Hec, si dictis→fiducis, luis→lues), and a translation that is often confused about who is speaking. The title describes a different work (the prose Vita Scipionis), so a reader looking for that life will not find it.

title: Ioannis Boccatii de Certaldo insigne opus De claris mulieribus
shelf_note: Boccaccio's De claris mulieribus (Bern 1539) is humanist biography. It has no tradition or collection assigned and is outside the core shelves, though a reasonable humanist adjunct.
structure_note: Pages 46, 90 and 135 run in order (Iole, Veturia, Mariamne leading into 'DE CLEO.'). 183 of 184 pages have OCR and 176 are translated. Nothing else stands out.

book_verdict: A clean printed text with mostly fluent translation. On two of the three pages, misreads flow straight into the English: Iole 'lived out' instead of avenging her father's death, and Herod is 'not a noble' instead of 'not a Jew'. A careful reader would be misled on these points.

title: Temperamentum Vastationis Bellicae (Küpffender / Reuter, Wittenberg 1677)
shelf_note: A Wittenberg disputation on the law of war (devastation, ius gentium). It has no tradition assigned and sits outside the esoteric/early-science shelves.
structure_note: Only 16 of 25 pages are translated and 24 have OCR, so about a third of a short dissertation has no English. place_published is 'Berlin', but the title page says Wittenberg, and Berlin is the holding library (SBB). This is a catalogue slip (I7).

ocr_errors.ocr: Deuteronomio XX, 12. ... Floro Libro II. capite 20. ... Disputatio
ocr_errors.image: Deut. XX, 12. ... Floro lib. II. c. 20. ... Disput.
ocr_errors.problem: the printed abbreviations in the references are silently expanded

tr_errors.source: nunquam autem tali vastatione obtinebitur, quae oppugnandorum vi- [page ends]
tr_errors.english: but it will never be obtained by such devastation that does not diminish the strength of those being attacked, nor can it take away their abundance of resources.
tr_errors.problem: the page breaks mid-word. The translation completes the sentence with a verb and a whole clause ('nor can it take away their abundance of resources') that are not on this page. Whether the guess matches the next page cannot be verified here

ocr_errors.problem: 'dominium' (public authority) read as 'dominum'. The translation then says 'the public lord'

tr_errors.source: per dominium publicum
tr_errors.english: is permitted by the public lord
tr_errors.problem: the sense is 'by right of public dominion'

other.note: Hornius's quotation is set as a markdown blockquote. It is run-in text on the page

book_verdict: Excellent OCR and a faithful translation of a dense legal disputation. The one serious slip is a page-end sentence finished with text not on the page. The book is a third untranslated, and its place of publication is wrong.

title: Clavicula Salomonis Regis
shelf_note: An 18th-century Latin manuscript of the Key of Solomon. This is core grimoire material, though no tradition is set on the record.
structure_note: Page 122 is a plate leaf: a pale blue paper roundel is pasted where a pentacle would be, and faint lines show through it. The text visible below the roundel is show-through from the other side of the leaf, not writing on this page. 228 of 245 pages are translated, which fits the plates being skipped or described.

tr_errors.problem: a redundant inserted note

ocr_errors.image: show-through from the other side of the leaf, beneath a pasted blue paper roundel
ocr_errors.problem: show-through is described as faded text on this page, and the pasted roundel is not mentioned

other.note: a plate page is given a description and an <unclear> block in the translation pane, plus a summary claiming it is 'consistent with the protective seals found elsewhere in the manuscript', an unverified claim

book_verdict: A clean, faithful read of a legible 18th-century hand. The text pages are showcase quality. The plate page is described rather than transcribed, with minor over-description.
